elements.element: A total aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY,” making the cap mutual.

elements.element: The cap’s fee component includes fees both paid and payable.
elements.evidence: The clause includes amounts “PAID OR PAYABLE,” but uses all “AMOUNTS” paid or payable by Ono rather than limiting the calculation to fees.

elements.element: The cap’s fee component is calculated over the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The lookback is the 12 months preceding “THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM,” not the 12 months preceding the claim.

elements.element: The cap uses the greater of the 12-month fee component and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly uses the greater of the stated 12-month amount and USD 1,000,000, although the amount and timing components do not precisely match the preferred formulation.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The clause states that neither party shall be liable for indirect damages suffered by the other party.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The clause states that neither party shall be liable for consequential damages suffered by the other party.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” expressly includes a party’s breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10, excluding those claims from the aggregate cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No data protection carve-out appears in the definition of “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No security-obligations carve-out appears in the definition of “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: The aggregate-cap carve-out covers only indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2. The existing clause separately identifies indemnities under Article 10, but those indemnities are omitted from “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and therefore remain subject to the aggregate cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and is also excluded from the pre-existing damages limitation.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Willful misconduct is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and is also excluded from the pre-existing damages limitation.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS,” so it is outside the aggregate cap.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other party’s intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no express carve-out for infringement of the other party’s intellectual property.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations do not constitute damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Ono’s payment obligations under Article VI “SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE ‘DAMAGES’ FOR PURPOSES OF THIS SECTION.”

elements.element: A total aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY,” making the cap mutual.

elements.element: The mutual cap equals 12 months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of 12 months’ amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, rather than a cap equal to 12 months’ fees; it also measures the period before the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Only indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2 are excluded from the aggregate cap, while indemnities under Article 10—expressly referenced in the existing clause—are not included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS.”

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party’s breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10 is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS.”

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS.”

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Willful misconduct is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS.”

result.reason: Neither position is fully satisfied. The preferred position is missing data-protection, security, complete indemnification, and IP-infringement carve-outs, and its fee basis and claim-based lookback are not followed. The fallback also fails because the cap is not equal to 12 months’ fees and not all identified indemnities are uncapped. The amendment generally leaves unrelated terms intact and introduces no direct contradiction, but it is not minimal because it does not reach either complete position. Drafting quality is reduced by the mismatch between “amounts” and fees, the event-based rather than claim-based trigger, and the inconsistent treatment of Article 10 indemnities.
